newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to rule on Mineralbank insolvency end-Mar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to rule on Mineralbank insolvency end-Mar.

text.p: The Sofia City Court is to rule on an insolvency case against state-owned Mineralbank filed by the Bulgarian National Bank by end-March, a Mineralbank sequestrator said on Wednesday.
"The court decided to rule on the case by the end of the month," Dimitar Zhelyazkov told reporters.

The court had accepted the reports of three experts on the bank's financial state as of May 31 when the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) opened the bankruptcy procedure against Mineralbank, said Zhelyazkov.
The BNB put Mineralbank in receivership on May 17, 1996 due to a danger of insolvency, dismissed its management and appointed sequestrators. The suit was filed two weeks later.

Mineralbank is among the 15 local private and state banks against which the BNB has opened insolvency suits in two waves in May and October last year. Only one of them has been ruled insolvent so far.

Last June Mineralbank failed to honour maturity payments on seven-year samurai bonds worth a total of five billion yen issued in 1989. The Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) was a lead arranger for the issue.
Former Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov told Japanese creditors in June that the Bulgarian government would not honour maturity payments on the bonds either.
"...the fact that the state is a shareholder in Mineralbank, which is a joint stock company, does not mean the state should take on additional guarantees for Mineralbank's obligations," Kostov said.
Mineralbank is 80 percent owned by the government.
The IBJ's Kiyoshi Watanabe has said Bulgaria's decision to treat Mineralbank as a private commercial bank for which it held no responsibility was a breach of international business practice.
In addition to the bonds, Mineralbank also owes some $100 million worth of loans to the IBJ. The interest on the loans has not been paid since the start of 1996.
IBJ officials have said they were willing to discuss various options for overcoming the dispute, including a possible rescheduling of payments.
Mineralbank's total debts to foreign banks amount to $240 million, including the $150 million of bonds and loans owed to the banks grouped in the IBJ.

Mineralbank, set up as an investment bank by Bulgaria's former communist regime in the 1980s, had racked up losses of 8.6 billion levs by the end of 1995, its annual report showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
